questions.question: Which two fellow King's Men actors and sharers dedicated Shakespeare's 1623 First Folio to the Earls of Pembroke and Montgomery?
questions.explanation: Heminges and Condell gathered Shakespeare's prompt-books and manuscripts to publish the First Folio in 1623.

questions.question: How many plays in Shakespeare's 1623 First Folio had never previously appeared in print in any quarto edition?
questions.explanation: Eighteen plays including Macbeth, The Tempest, Julius Caesar, and Twelfth Night were preserved exclusively in the First Folio.

questions.question: In 'The King James Bible' (1611), how many scholarly translators were appointed by the crown, organized into six separate translation companies?
questions.explanation: Though roughly 54 were initially nominated, 47 active scholars worked in six committees across Westminster, Oxford, and Cambridge.

questions.question: Which famous verse eulogy by Ben Jonson prefacing the 1623 First Folio contains the line 'He was not of an age, but for all time!'?
options: To the Memory of My Beloved the Author, Mr. William Shakespeare
questions.explanation: Jonson's generous commemorative poem hailed Shakespeare as the Sweet Swan of Avon, triumphing over Greek and Roman rivals.

questions.question: In Francis Bacon's 'Novum Organum' (1620), which class of Idols arises from the illusions and ambiguities of human language and social discourse?
questions.explanation: Idola Fori arise from words that obstruct understanding, described by Bacon as the most troublesome of all intellectual errors.

questions.question: In Francis Bacon's 'Novum Organum', which class of Idols stems from human nature itself and the inherent limitations of our sensory organs?
questions.explanation: Idola Tribus are errors rooted in human nature, distorting reality like an uneven mirror reflecting rays.

questions.question: What is the name of the utopian Pacific island commonwealth described in Francis Bacon's posthumous 1627 philosophical fable?
questions.explanation: In New Atlantis, European travelers stumble upon Bensalem, a Christian island governed by scientific wisdom.

questions.question: What is the title of John Donne's 1610 prose treatise arguing that English Roman Catholics could lawfully swear the Oath of Allegiance?
questions.explanation: Pseudo-Martyr pleased King James I by asserting that Catholics who died for refusing the civil oath were not true martyrs.

questions.question: Which 1611 satirical prose work by John Donne stages a debate in Hell where Ignatius of Loyola contends with Copernicus, Paracelsus, and Machiavelli?
questions.explanation: In Ignatius His Conclave, Donne bitterly mocks Jesuit ambition, showing Lucifer terrified of Ignatius usurping his throne.

questions.question: Which 1611 philosophical poem by John Donne laments the death of young Elizabeth Drury and contains the famous line 'New Philosophy calls all in doubt'?
options: An Anatomy of the World: The First Anniversary
questions.explanation: The First Anniversary laments the decay of the universe, mourning the collapse of the Ptolemaic order before Copernican science.

questions.question: In John Donne's 'A Valediction: Forbidding Mourning', what mathematical instrument provides the central metaphysical conceit for the lovers' souls?
options: A pair of stiff twin compasses
questions.explanation: Donne compares the lovers' souls to a compass, where the fixed foot leans and hearkens after the moving foot's circle.

questions.question: In John Donne's 'The Flea', what three lives are wittily joined inside the insect's body before the mistress kills it?
options: The speaker's life, the lady's life, and the flea's own life
The priest, the bishop, and the Pope
The lover, the husband, and the priest
The father, the mother, and the unborn child
questions.explanation: Donne argues that since their blood is mingled within the flea, they are more than married, making guilt or shame absurd.

questions.question: Which early 17th-century poet and diplomat authored the famous definition: 'An ambassador is an honest man sent to lie abroad for the good of his country'?
questions.explanation: Sir Henry Wotton penned the punning maxim in Augsburg in 1604, temporarily displeasing King James I.

questions.question: Which elder brother of George Herbert published 'De Veritate' in 1624, earning recognition as the 'Father of English Deism'?
options: Edward Herbert, Lord Herbert of Cherbury
questions.explanation: Lord Herbert of Cherbury's De Veritate posited universal religious truths founded upon natural reason rather than revelation.

questions.question: Which Jacobean court scandal of 1613–1616 involved the slow poisoning in the Tower of an author who opposed the Earl of Somerset's marriage?
options: The Murder of Sir Thomas Overbury
questions.explanation: Sir Thomas Overbury was poisoned in the Tower for opposing Robert Carr's union with Frances Howard.

questions.question: Which 1614 collection, expanded after the author's murder, popularized the 'Theophrastan character' sketch of English social types?
questions.explanation: Overbury's Characters presented witty, satirical portraits of social types like the fair milkmaid and pedantic scholar.

questions.question: Which 1605 court masque by Ben Jonson and Inigo Jones provoked court controversy by having Queen Anne and her ladies appear in blackface?
questions.explanation: Queen Anne commissioned Jonson to present African nymphs desiring transformation by the sun of Britannia.

questions.question: Which structural theatrical innovation was invented by Ben Jonson for his 1609 court entertainment 'The Masque of Queens'?
options: The Orchestra pit beneath the stage
The Epilogue spoken by a boy actor
The Antimasque (a chaotic, grotesque spectacle preceding the main harmonious masque)
questions.explanation: Jonson introduced the antimasque of ugly witches to contrast with the noble queens, establishing aesthetic duality.

questions.question: Which 1605 stage comedy written by Chapman, Jonson, and Marston included anti-Scottish satire that caused Jonson's temporary imprisonment?
questions.explanation: Eastward Ho satirised King James I's newly created Scottish knights and colonial promotion in Virginia.

questions.question: Which Scottish poet hosted Ben Jonson in 1618–1619, recording Jonson's candid, biting literary judgments in his private journals?
questions.explanation: Drummond's Conversations preserves Jonson's frank opinions, including his verdict that Donne deserved hanging for not keeping accent.

questions.question: In Ben Jonson's 'The Alchemist', which lecherous and greedy knight dreams of bathing in milk and dining on barbel's roes and pheasants' tongues?
questions.explanation: Sir Epicure Mammon delivers magnificent, sensual speeches imagining the boundless luxury the Philosopher's Stone will bring.

questions.question: In 'The Alchemist', what is the name of the puritan pastor from Amsterdam who seeks the Philosopher's Stone to fund his sect?
questions.explanation: Tribulation Wholesome, an elder of Amsterdam, rationalises cheating and coining money for the good of the brethren.

questions.question: Which Roman tragedy by Ben Jonson, staged by the King's Men in 1603, was censured before the Privy Council for suspected treasonable allusions?
questions.explanation: Sejanus dramatised corrupt tyrannical favorites in Imperial Rome, causing Jonson to be summoned before the Council.

questions.question: In John Webster's 'The White Devil' (1612), who is the defiant Italian noblewoman tried before Cardinal Monticelso in the trial scene?
questions.explanation: Vittoria defends herself brilliantly in the arraignment scene, claiming her accusers' charity is like the moon, full of spots.

questions.question: In 'The White Devil', which unprincipled brother of Vittoria serves as Brachiano's pander and dies mocking his murderers?
questions.explanation: Flamineo is Webster's cynical malcontent tool-villain who murders his brother Marcello and dies unrepentant.

questions.question: In Webster's 'The Duchess of Malfi', what is the name of the faithful household steward whom the Duchess secretly marries?
questions.explanation: Antonio Bologna is the honest steward whose secret marriage to the Duchess produces three children before their doom.

questions.question: In 'The Duchess of Malfi', what gruesome psychological torment is presented to the Duchess by Duke Ferdinand in the dark?
options: A poisoned mirror reflecting her skull
A cage of poisonous scorpions and severed tongues
A procession of lepers demanding her royal gown
A dead man's severed hand wearing a wedding ring and wax figures of her slain family
questions.explanation: Ferdinand gives her a dead hand to kiss and displays artificial wax figures of Antonio and her children dead.

questions.question: What famous defiant line is spoken by the Duchess of Malfi immediately prior to her execution by Bosola's stranglers?
options: Cover her face; mine eyes dazzle; she died young
We are merely the stars' tennis-balls
I am Duchess of Malfi still
My soul, like to a ship in a black storm
questions.explanation: The Duchess confronts death with magnificent stoic dignity, uttering her immortal declaration of identity.

questions.question: In Thomas Middleton's 'Women Beware Women' (c. 1621), which aristocratic pastime is used as an allegory to mask the Duke's seduction of Bianca?
options: A masked hunting excursion in the forest
A fencing match with poisoned foils
A game of bowls on the royal lawns
A game of chess played between Livia and Leantio's mother
questions.explanation: Livia distracts the mother in a game of chess where moves on the board allegorise the Duke seducing Bianca upstairs.

questions.question: In Middleton and Rowley's 'The Changeling', what physical deformity makes Beatrice-Joanna loathe De Flores before her crime binds them?
options: A severe hunchback and withered arm
A wooden leg and glass eye
A cleft palate and hairless skull
His dog-bitten, scarred, and pimpled face
questions.explanation: Beatrice-Joanna repeatedly recoils from De Flores's facial blemishes, calling him a poison to her sight.

questions.question: Which Jacobean tragicomedy by Beaumont and Fletcher centers on the page Bellario, who is revealed to be Euphrasia in disguise?
questions.explanation: In Philaster, Bellario serves the prince out of unexpressed love, revealing her female identity to resolve jealousy.

questions.question: In Beaumont and Fletcher's 'The Maid's Tragedy' (c. 1610), which bride reveals on her wedding night that she is the King's mistress?
questions.explanation: Evadne refuses to consummate her marriage with Amintor, revealing her secret arrangement with the King.

questions.question: Which playwright composed the tragic masterpiece 'The Broken Heart' (printed 1633), set in classical Laconia/Sparta?
questions.explanation: John Ford's The Broken Heart dramatises the stoic suffering and grief of Penthea and Calantha in Sparta.

questions.question: In Cyril Tourneur's 'The Atheist's Tragedy' (1611), how is the villainous atheist D'Amville killed at the execution scaffold?
options: He is pushed off the battlements by Charlemont
He accidentally strikes out his own brains with the executioner's axe
He is struck by a bolt of divine lightning
He drinks a poisoned flask of holy water
questions.explanation: D'Amville raises the axe to execute Charlemont but stumbles and shatters his own skull, proving God's justice.

questions.question: Which 1612 treatise by Thomas Heywood defended the dignity, moral utility, and classical pedigree of the theatrical profession?
options: Short View of the Immorality of the Stage
questions.explanation: Heywood argued that drama educates the illiterate in history and inspires citizens to civic virtue.

questions.question: Which Shakespearean play was being performed on June 29, 1613, when theatrical cannons ignited the thatched roof and burned the Globe to the ground?
questions.explanation: During Cardinal Wolsey's masque scene in Henry VIII, stage cannon wadding set the thatch alight, destroying the Globe.

questions.question: In Shakespeare's 'Measure for Measure' (1604), which puritanical deputy ruler enforces the death penalty for fornication in Vienna?
questions.explanation: Angelo condemns Claudio to death for impregnating Juliet, then attempts to extort Isabella's virginity for his pardon.

questions.question: In 'Measure for Measure', what theatrical bed-trick is engineered by Duke Vincentio to save Isabella from Angelo's lust?
options: Substituting Mariana of the Moated Grange in the dark bedchamber
Disguising Juliet as a Novice nun
Poisoning Angelo's nightcup of spiced wine
questions.explanation: Mariana, Angelo's jilted betrothed, takes Isabella's place in the dark garden house to consummate their marriage contract.

questions.question: Which Shakespearean Roman tragedy centers on the patrician Caius Martius, who joins with the Volscian Aufidius against his ungrateful city?
questions.explanation: Coriolanus despises the Roman plebeians, waging war against Rome until swayed by his formidable mother Volumnia.

questions.question: In 'Coriolanus', who is the towering Roman matriarch whose eloquent pleading dissuades Coriolanus from burning Rome to ashes?
questions.explanation: Volumnia kneels before her son, declaring he must tread upon his mother's womb to assault Rome.

questions.question: Which Shakespearean romance, omitted from the 1623 First Folio, was included in the Third Folio of 1664 based on a 1609 quarto?
questions.explanation: Pericles, largely co-authored with George Wilkins, was excluded from the First Folio but added to the 1664 Third Folio.

questions.question: In Shakespeare's 'Cymbeline', which villainous Italian trickster hides in a chest to inspect the mole under Imogen's breast?
questions.explanation: Iachimo emerges from a trunk in Imogen's chamber to note intimate bodily details to falsely claim her infidelity.

questions.question: In 'The Winter's Tale', what famously bizarre stage direction occurs in Act III when Antigonus abandons the baby Perdita on the coast of Bohemia?
options: He falls into a pit of vipers
Thunder and lightning; the ship sinks
questions.explanation: Exit, pursued by a bear is Shakespeare's most famous and unexpected stage direction, bridging tragedy and romance.

questions.question: What is the name of the roguish singing peddler, ballad-monger, and pickpocket who roams the sheep-shearing feast in 'The Winter's Tale'?
questions.explanation: Autolycus describes himself as a snapper-up of unconsidered trifles, selling songs and picking rural pockets.

questions.question: To which two aristocratic brothers, described as the Incomparable Pair of Brethren, did Heminges and Condell dedicate the First Folio?
options: William Herbert (Earl of Pembroke) and Philip Herbert (Earl of Montgomery)
questions.explanation: The First Folio was dedicated to the Pembroke brothers for their long patronage and affection for Shakespeare.

questions.question: Which engraved portrait of William Shakespeare, praised by Ben Jonson, was included on the title page of the 1623 First Folio?
options: The Droeshout Portrait (engraved by Martin Droeshout)
questions.explanation: Martin Droeshout's copperplate engraving is one of only two authentic contemporary likenesses of Shakespeare.

questions.question: In George Chapman's 'The Conspiracy and Tragedy of Charles, Duke of Byron' (1608), what historic foreign court serves as the setting?
options: The royal French court of King Henry IV
The Imperial court of Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II
The papal court of Pope Clement VIII in Rome
The ducal palace of Florence under the Medici
questions.explanation: Chapman dramatised contemporary French politics, provoking diplomatic protests from the French ambassador.

questions.question: Which 1623 poem by Ben Jonson, titled 'An Execration upon Vulcan', commemorates the catastrophic loss of his personal library by:
options: A devastating fire that destroyed his books and unfinished manuscripts
Confiscation by puritan authorities in London
Theft by rival theater playwrights in Shoreditch
Shipwreck in the Irish Channel during a voyage to Scotland
questions.explanation: Jonson curses the Roman god of fire Vulcan for burning his translation of Horace and historical research.

questions.question: Which Jacobean poet composed the Latin epigram collection 'Epigrammata' (1606–1612), achieving fame as the 'British Martial' across Europe?
questions.explanation: John Owen's sharp Latin epigrams were admired across continental Europe and translated into multiple vernaculars.

questions.question: What is the name of the ancient British king whose reign forms the backdrop for Shakespeare's romance 'Cymbeline'?
questions.explanation: Cymbeline was an actual historic British Celtic chieftain who ruled Britain during the reign of Augustus Caesar.
